name: Madhuri (Shonga-tser) Lake
tagline: A 3,708 m army-guarded lake with drowned tree trunks, near Bum La
best_time: April to June and October–November, when the road is usually clear and the lake is not frozen over.

permit.indians: Tourist eILP plus the special permit issued in Tawang for the Bum La area, which covers the Madhuri Lake road; army checks on the way.
permit.foreigners: Generally not permitted; the lake lies on the restricted Bum La road near the border. Confirm with your operator.

ideal_stay: 2 to 3 hours as part of the Bum La day from Tawang
meta_description: Madhuri Lake (Sangetsar Tso) guide: 3,708 m lake near Bum La, permit from Tawang, army cafe, road conditions, best months and how to plan the day.
quick_answer: Madhuri Lake, officially Sangetsar Tso and once called Shonga-tser, is a 3,708 m lake about 35 to 40 km by road north of Tawang, near Bum La. It formed in the 1950 earthquake and is guarded by the army. Indians need the eILP and the Bum La area permit from Tawang; foreigners are generally not allowed.
intro: The lake got its popular name in 1997, when a song from the film Koyla was shot here with Madhuri Dixit. Locals and the army still call it Sangetsar Tso. It was created when the great Assam–Tibet earthquake of 1950 brought down rock and forest to dam a stream, and the grey trunks of the drowned trees still stand in the water.

It sits at 3,708 m in a bowl of rock and fir forest, a few kilometres off the main Bum La road. The army maintains the lakeside path and runs a small cafe where we have had some of the best hot momos and tea of any Tawang trip, especially welcome after the wind at Bum La.
Most people visit on the same day as Bum La, turning off at the junction on the way back to Tawang. The road is narrow and rough, and only local SUVs named on the permit may drive it.

highlights.name: The drowned forest
highlights.text: Bare tree trunks standing in the water, left from the 1950 earthquake that formed the lake.

highlights.name: Army cafe
highlights.text: A small army-run kitchen by the lake serving tea, coffee and momos when it is open.

highlights.name: Lakeside walk
highlights.text: A short, maintained path along the shore with wooden bridges and viewpoints.

highlights.name: Koyla connection
highlights.text: The lake's popular name comes from a 1997 film song shot here, and the story is told to every visitor.

highlights.name: Route through high lakes
highlights.text: The drive passes PT Tso and many smaller tarns between 3,700 and 4,500 m.

things_to_do: Walk the shoreline path and photograph the drowned tree trunks
Warm up with tea and momos at the army cafe
Combine with Bum La and PT Tso in a single day from Tawang
Watch for snow on the surrounding ridges from October to May
Carry binoculars for birds on the water and in the fir forest
Listen to the soldiers' short account of the lake's history
how_to_reach: Madhuri Lake is about 35 to 40 km from Tawang by the army road towards Bum La, turning off at a junction several kilometres below the pass. The drive takes around 2 to 2.5 hours each way because the surface is broken and single-lane in parts. Only local Tawang SUVs listed on the permit are allowed, and recent circuit prices for Bum La, PT Tso and Madhuri Lake have been Rs 5,500 to 6,000 per vehicle. To reach Tawang, allow two days from Guwahati or about 320 km from Tezpur. Check current status before you travel.
where_to_stay: There is no accommodation near the lake; you return to Tawang the same day. Stay in a Tawang hotel or homestay that routinely arranges Bum La area permits and local SUVs, which makes the day easier. The upper part of town, along the monastery road, is handy for an early start. From October to April choose a room with a heater and ask for an early breakfast or a packed one, since you should leave by 7 am.
tips: The lake is covered by the same special permit process as Bum La; file it a day ahead in Tawang
Do not photograph army posts or vehicles; ask the soldiers what is allowed
Afternoon cloud rolls in quickly, so plan to be at the lake by early afternoon
The lake can freeze from December to March and the road may be closed by snow
Carry cash; there are no ATMs beyond Tawang
Wear waterproof boots; the lakeside path is often wet or icy

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Madhuri Lake?
faqs.a: Yes. Besides the Arunachal Pradesh eILP, you need the special permit issued in Tawang for the Bum La area, which covers the Madhuri Lake road. Hotels and local drivers usually file it a day ahead at the Deputy Commissioner's office with copies of your ID and eILP. Army posts check it on the way. Check current status before you travel.

Generally no. Madhuri Lake lies on the restricted Bum La road near the Line of Actual Control, and the special permit is issued to Indian citizens. Foreign nationals with a Protected Area Permit can visit Tawang, the monastery and Sela Pass instead. Confirm the latest position with your tour operator, as rules can change.

faqs.q: Why is it called Madhuri Lake?
faqs.a: The lake's official name is Sangetsar Tso, earlier written Shonga-tser. It became known as Madhuri Lake after a song from the 1997 film Koyla, starring Madhuri Dixit and Shah Rukh Khan, was filmed here. The name stuck with tourists, although the army and local people still use Sangetsar Tso.

faqs.q: How far is Madhuri Lake from Tawang?
faqs.a: It is about 35 to 40 km from Tawang by road, which takes around 2 to 2.5 hours each way on a rough army road. Most people visit it on the same day as Bum La and PT Tso, leaving Tawang around 7 am and returning by late afternoon in a local SUV.

faqs.q: When is Madhuri Lake frozen or closed by snow?
faqs.a: The lake often freezes from December to March, and heavy snow can close the road for days or weeks in that period. April to June and October to November usually give open roads and unfrozen water. Monsoon months bring cloud and slippery tracks. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is altitude sickness a concern at Madhuri Lake?
faqs.a: The lake is at 3,708 m and the Bum La road climbs higher, to about 4,600 m. Most visitors feel short of breath, and some get headaches. Spend at least one night in Tawang first, walk slowly, drink water and avoid alcohol the night before. Descend if symptoms worsen.

faqs.q: Is there food, mobile network or an ATM at Madhuri Lake?
faqs.a: There is a small army-run cafe serving tea and snacks when it is open, but no ATMs anywhere on the route, so carry cash from Tawang. Mobile signal is mostly absent on the Bum La road. Take water and a few snacks in case the cafe is closed.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Madhuri Lake?
faqs.a: April to June and October to November are the best months, with a better chance of an open road, blue water and snow on the surrounding ridges. Winter brings a frozen lake but frequent closures. June to September is monsoon, with cloud, rain and slippery roads that can stop vehicles.

faqs.q: Is Madhuri Lake suitable for children and senior citizens?
faqs.a: The lakeside path is short and gentle, so the lake itself is manageable. The challenge is the long, bumpy drive at high altitude. Healthy seniors and older children usually cope with warm layers and a slow pace, but we would skip the trip for infants or anyone with heart or breathing conditions.
